transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi, I'm Dora, a clinical conversational agent. Do you have any questions about your cataract surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can go back to light exercise, such as gardening, one week after surgery. However, you should avoid strenuous, heavy exercise, lifting heavy objects, pilates or yoga, or swimming for a month.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, thanks. Another question I have is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I can only help with questions about your cataract surgery recovery. I don't have information about specific eye gels. If you were using eye drops for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise. If you have questions about a specific eye gel, I recommend contacting your care team. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Alright, I'll check with my care team about that. Another thing I wanted to ask is, I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside. However, significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity, especially if your eye is also red and painful, is not normal and may need further assessment. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I have one last question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common for your vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation. This should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure it’s okay. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I don't have any more questions. Thank you for your help, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! So, just to confirm, all your questions have been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thanks again!

verdict.label: pass
verdict.reasoning: The agent successfully conveyed `normal_sensitivity_reassurance` and `mild_case_advice` in the turn starting with "It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light...". In the same turn, the agent also conveyed `escalation_criteria` by stating, "However, significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity, especially if your eye is also red and painful, is not normal and may need further assessment." All three points were covered.
